text: Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.
mechanism: With 1024 rows and labels set by 2-4 coordinates, once Δ≥0.1 the decision boundary is already fit; test CE is then set by logit scale on misclassified points, so anything that speeds fitting (depth, LN, ReLU kinks, larger lr) inflates confidence. Predicts the same reversal for optimizer Δ (K1021) and no reversal on XOR/spiral where the boundary is still being learned.

regime.note: 1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features; Δ per core rule

phase: Δ_shared<0.1: more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17; Δ_shared≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16 (counterexample q_87182b: more early LN in residual LeakyReLU won). Across Δ (mixed questions) prefer Δ≈0.1-0.3 over ≥3× larger (K1021).

text: Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
mechanism: Depth adds composed nonlinear capacity that, with only 1024 rows and 12+ noise coordinates, is spent fitting distractor structure once the data has been revisited many times; the overfit cost scales with epochs, not with Δ alone. So the Δ at which shallow-wide nets overtake deep ones falls as epochs rise (4→32). Predicts: at ≤4 epochs the K1009 Δ≥0.1 threshold holds; at Δ<0.03 nets are still boundary-limited and depth/LN help.

regime.note: one instance per family; depth confounded with width/LN; piecewise untested

phase: shallow(2-block) vs deep(4-block), Δ 0.03-0.1: 32 epochs → shallow 16/16 (ratio .59-.75); 4 epochs → 4/8 (.99). Corpus ≥16 epochs: Δ≥0.1 shallow 12/15 (.65); Δ<0.03 shallow 6/17 (1.04).

text: SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1019 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).
mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

text: Spiral coupled weight decay (two-spiral CE, 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024, CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than AdamW at the same wd or any wd=0 twin: controlled plain ReLU d2 w48 lr 3e-3: Adam wd1e-3 CE 0.003, wd1e-2 0.044 vs AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4, wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4 (AdamW beats Adam 12/12 cells, ratio 0.002-0.03); q_6a81f1 AdamW beat Adam (both wd1e-3) on 1-layer GELU w256. Rank coupled-Adam+wd below such twins regardless of β2. β2 alone flips with lr (0.95 better at lr≥1e-3 plain nets, 0.999 at 3e-4): weak tie-break. Not seen on bigram LM (q_e6d625).
mechanism: torch Adam adds wd·w to the gradient before dividing by √v. Once the spiral is fit, data gradients→~0, so the decay term dominates both numerator and v and Adam takes ~lr-sized normalized steps toward zero, capping weight norm and logit margin (CE floor ~1e-3). AdamW shrinks by lr·wd·w (~1e-6/step), negligible. Predicts harm grows with wd, lr and T, and vanishes when data gradients stay large (noisy-label bigram LM, under-trained 3-turn spirals).

regime.note: one controlled architecture + q_6a81f1, q_682517; RMSprop/Adagrad coupled wd untested; 2-3 turn spirals untested

phase: AdamW(wd) vs Adam(coupled wd), same lr/net, spiral: wd1e-3 ratio ~0.03, wd1e-2 ~0.002 (12/12). β2 .999 vs .95 (same wd): lr 3e-3 ratio 5.8, 1e-3 24 (0.95 wins); lr 3e-4 ratio 0.36 (0.999 wins); with LN signs mixed.

text: TABULAR classification Δ sweet spot vs EPOCHS (synthetic, 1024 rows; E=total_samples_seen/1024; core-rule Δ). Below Δ≈0.03 more Δ wins at E=4 (lab 56/56). The CE-optimal Δ then SHRINKS with E on smooth_additive: E=4 ≈0.25 (Δ0.77 lost to 0.26, 3/3 controlled); E=16 ≈0.08 (controlled 2/2; q_c1581a RMSprop 1e-4×256 bs64 Δ0.026 beat Adam 1e-3 Δ0.26 and AdamW 3e-3 Δ0.77); E=32 ≈0.05-0.15: Δ≥0.5 loses (lab 24/28) and ≥3× more loses 1/15 once small Δ≥0.03. sparse_interaction: optimum ≈0.25 at E 4-16, 0.15 at E 32; larger loses once small Δ≥0.1 (lab 5/33, CE ×1.44). piecewise tolerates more (larger wins 10/10 at E=16). Then use architecture (K1009/K1033).
mechanism: Once the boundary is learned, extra displacement inflates logit norm and fits distractor directions on only 1024 rows; test CE punishes confident errors. Bigger batches over more epochs give cleaner gradients, so each unit of Δ fits training rows faster and the overfit point comes at smaller Δ. Sparse interactions need more movement to find the feature pair (higher optimum); axis-aligned piecewise boundaries keep gaining from sharper logits.
